children: Oil falls in early Asian trade. U.S. crude oil inventories rose more than expected in a second straight weekly build, according to data released Wednesday by the EIA. Commercial crude oil stocks excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve increased by 3.4 million barrels in the week ended Nov. 13, the data showed. Crude stockpiles were expected to have risen by 1 million barrels, according to a WSJ survey of analysts. Front-month WTI crude oil futures are 0.6% lower at $82.77 per barrel. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
